newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fairfax concerned at break-up speculation.
newsitem.headline: Fairfax concerned at break-up speculation.

text.p: John Fairfax Holdings Ltd chairman Sir Laurence Street said on Friday that there would be widespread community concern if a new national media policy allowed the newspaper publisher to be broken up.

"I think it's something that all Australians should be alarmed at," Street said on Australian Broadcasting Corp radio, referring to widespread speculation that the government would allow Fairfax to be sold to Kerry Packer after he sold one of the key Fairfax publications.
"I don't know where it (the speculation) is coming from ... the story is now so prominent that I think it's got to be taken seriously," Street said.

Fairfax publishes the Sydney Morning Herald and Melbourne Age broadsheet daily newspapers, as well as the Australian Financial Review daily newspaper and the Business Review Weekly magazine, among other titles.

The Howard government was expected to this week consider changes to the media rules which would remove the cross-media restrictions which prevented one person from owning television stations and newspapers in the same metropolitan market.

Kerry Packer, the owner of the top-ranked Nine television network through his Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, is a 15 percent shareholder in Fairfax and has long expressed an interest in taking over the company.
Executives from London-based publisher Pearson Plc and its half-owned The Economist magazine have met with Australian government officials this week to discuss the planned media rule changes.
Some Fairfax papers and The Australian newspaper have variously reported that Pearson was keen on acquiring The Australian Financial Review newspaper.
